issues.legal_issue: A tribunal may recall an order approving a resolution plan under its inherent powers on limited grounds that would cause a gross failure of justice.

An application to recall an order approving a resolution plan is not barred by time when filed within the applicable limitation period, including any period excluded by a court-ordered suspension of limitation.
A resolution plan must give due consideration to a creditor’s verifiable claim even when submitted in a form different from the form prescribed for the creditor’s proper category.
A resolution plan must recognize a creditor’s statutory charge over the corporate debtor’s assets and account for the creditor as a secured creditor.

A resolution plan that proposes to use land owned by a third party must demonstrate its feasibility and viability, including the necessary approvals from the landowner or relevant statutory authority.
